Subject: Acero Health — customer-driven probe: window, scripts, and IP allowlist

Hi Jack / Sara,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on the SLO targets and the test approach.  Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all on the same page: 

Summary from our discovery
- Target p95 latency for text-generation endpoint: <= 220 ms for 512-token responses
- Target sustained throughput: 40 req/s for a 5m window (customer traffic multiplexing)
- Streaming requirement: up to 50 concurrent streaming sessions with partial-token flush every 150-200ms
- Concurrency probe: ramps to 100 total simultaneous sessions to validate graceful degradation

Requested next steps
1) Customer-led dry run using your k6/Locust scripts in the window you choose — we can allowlist IP ranges and provide a test account
2) You provide the script (or we can adapt) and a traffic matrix (mix of streaming vs non-streaming, payload sizes)
3) Redwood will attach observability hooks (traces, per-token latency) and a temporary forwarding policy so you can push from your env

Can you confirm: preferred test window (UTC options this week), who will run the test from Acero, and whether you want us to start with the k6 version or Locust?  

I attached a starter k6 script and a template for the test-account creds — Marissa and Ben are looped in to help with allowlist and monitoring.

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184

Attachments: acero_k6_script_v1.js (application/javascript), acero_test_account_creds.txt (text/plain)
From: Jack Owens <jack.owens@acerohealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Mills <sara@loadscout.io>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acero Health — customer-driven probe: window, scripts, and IP allowlist

Hi Neha,

Appreciate the summary — that matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications before we lock a window: 

- Streaming: our consumer-facing app opens ~30 streams concurrent during peak. For the probe, we want to validate up to 50 concurrent active streams (gradual ramp). The partial-token flush cadence is important; we will keep 150ms target.
- Concurrency ramp plan: we'll start at 10 concurrent sessions, step up by 10 every 3 minutes until 100, then hold three 5-minute plateaus at 50/75/100 to collect steady-state metrics.
- Payloads: 70% short prompts (<= 64 tokens), 30% long (400-600 tokens).

We can run a dry-run Friday 2028-03-30 18:00–19:30 UTC (preferred) or Monday 2028-04-02 02:00–03:30 UTC (backup). Sara will run the k6 harness from our environment; she confirmed she can share the exact script.

Please confirm the IP ranges to allowlist and any rate-limiting rules that could interfere. Also want to confirm whether the test account will be rate-limited per-token or per-request (we prefer per-request with a high cap).

Thanks,
Jack Owens
Director of Platform Engineering | Acero Health
jack.owens@acerohealth.com

Hi team / Jack / Sara,

Thanks — I updated the starter k6 script to reflect Jack's ramp plan and the payload mix.  Changes made:
- added streaming session hooks (k6 websocket wrapper) and 150ms flush emulation
- implemented the 10->100 ramp with 3min steps and 5-min holds at plateaus
- payload selector to get 70/30 short/long distribution

Attachments included:
- acero_k6_script_v1.js (updated) — please review and confirm runs clean on your side
- ip-allowlist.csv — CIDR ranges below that Acero should open (we'll only accept traffic from these during the window)
- acero_test_account_creds.txt — temporary API key (expires 2028-03-31 02:00 UTC) and usage notes

IP ranges (summary):
- 34.210.128.0/24
- 52.14.200.0/24
- 18.196.32.0/24

Notes on rate limits: we provisioned a per-request cap of 600 rps tied to the test key but configured token-level throttling disabled for the key (so you won't hit token throttles during the scaling window). If you prefer conservative caps, tell us and we can lower to 300 rps.

Observability: Redwood will push an ad-hoc dashboard (link below) and a temporary trace-export endpoint.  Ben added the monitoring hooks and will join the Friday run.

Proposed run playbook (Friday 2028-03-30 18:00–19:30 UTC)
- 17:45 UTC: allowlist ingress confirmed, test key active
- 17:50 UTC: k6 warmup (low concurrency) for 5 minutes
- 18:00 UTC: official ramp begins (10 -> 100)
- 18:45 UTC: steady-state runs and streaming validation
- 19:20 UTC: controlled wind-down and post-run data export

Jack / Sara: if that works, please reply with a one-line confirm and the external IP(s) you'll be running from (or confirm you'll use the k6 Cloud).

Marissa Cole
